X1.name: Consumer Proposition Test: Use Case vs Brand Premium
X1.method: Online survey with simulated product offers. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: (A) a small-scale landscaping use case proposition (e.g., 'Deere's new 2-cylinder landscaping tractor: 30-minute mowing, $1,200') or (B) a premium brand proposition (e.g., 'Own the trusted Deere brand: $1,500 lawn tractor'). Both offer the same basic model with a 5% discount. Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale and stated willingness to pay.
X1.sample: 300 U.S. adults recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and region to reflect 1962 demographics. 150 per condition.
X1.measure: Purchase intent score (1‑2) and willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary: stated reason for choice (use case vs brand).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Condition A will achieve higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Condition B.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Condition B will achieve higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Condition A.

X1.decision_rule: If purchase intent for Condition A exceeds Condition B by at least 1.5 points on a 7-point scale (i.e., A >= B + 1.5), proceed with a differentiated use‑case proposition. If Condition B exceeds Condition A by at least 1.5 points, proceed with a premium brand proposition. If the difference is ≥ 1.5 points, both conditions are considered; otherwise, no expansion is recommended.

final.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting small-scale landscaping, leveraging Deere’s existing tractor engineering. The evidence shows a prototype was built in 1959 and Deere evaluated competitive lawn tractors, but no consumer demand data exists. Proceed with a limited test to validate purchase intent for a use‑case proposition.
final.target_customer: Homeowners and small‑business owners in the United States who need a single machine for light landscaping tasks.
final.value_proposition: A dedicated, easy‑to‑use landscaping tractor that reduces tool switching and offers time savings, positioned as a convenient, efficient solution for small‑scale tasks.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Consumer Proposition Test (Use Case vs Brand Premium) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for a small‑scale landscaping proposition versus a premium brand proposition.
final.uncertainty: The size of the consumer market in 1962 and the actual willingness to pay for a differentiated model are unknown. Independent dealer adoption and stock levels for a new product line are also uncertain.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent for the premium brand proposition exceeds the use‑case proposition by at least 1.5 points, the recommendation would shift to a premium brand strategy.
If sales data from 1961‑95 show strong lawn mower demand, the case for a differentiated consumer proposition would strengthen.
If independent dealers show low interest in stocking a new product line, the investment case would weaken.

position.recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting status-conscious consumers, leveraging Deere's existing lawn and garden tractor engineering. Begin with a limited pilot to validate demand before full-scale rollout.

frame.objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeframe for any proposed experiment.
Must assess current reach to individual buyers and market demand for consumer‑focused products.
Evidence must justify investment; financial data is unavailable.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., small‑scale landscaping, hobby farming).
2) Expand existing dealer network to reach more individual buyers without a new product proposition.
3) No expansion: continue current business model with independent dealers and existing product line.
4) License tractor technology to third‑party manufacturers for consumer applications.
5) Partner with consumer brands to co‑develop and market a consumer‑focused product.

X1.name: Consumer Proposition vs Existing Dealer Sales Test
X1.method: Run a targeted online survey in two segments: Segment A (status-conscious consumers) and Segment B (small‑scale task users). Both segments will be offered a virtual preview of a differentiated consumer proposition (e.g., a compact, feature‑rich lawn mower) at a fixed price point. Segment A will also be offered a discounted version of the same product. Track two metrics per segment: (1) stated willingness to pay a premium (price premium over a baseline price) and (2) purchase intent (binary: would buy).
X1.sample: Segment A: 300 respondents (200 self‑identified as status‑conscious, 100 as utility‑focused). Segment B: 300 respondents (200 self‑identified as small‑scale task users, 100 as utility‑focused). Total 600 respondents, balanced by gender and region.
X1.measure: Average willingness to pay premium (segment A) and average purchase intent (binary) for the differentiated proposition.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Segment A will show a higher average willingness to pay premium than Segment B, indicating status-driven demand.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Segment B will show a higher average willingness to pay premium than Segment A, indicating utility-driven demand.

If the difference is less than 20 percentage points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and focus on expanding the existing dealer network. If the difference is not observed, conduct a separate test to differentiate between status and utility drivers.

X1.name: Segmented Purchase Intent Test
X1.method: Online survey with randomized exposure to a Deere lawn tractor description and a competitor lawn tractor description. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three segments: small-scale landscaping/hobby farming (n=200), affluent homeowners (n=200), and general consumers (n=200). Each segment sees its assigned description and a brief description of the competitor model. The survey measures purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and stated reason for choosing the product.
X1.sample: 800 respondents (400 per segment) recruited from a panel representing the target demographics (small‑scale users, affluent homeowners, and general consumers).
X1.measure: Purchase intent score for Deere versus competitor in each segment.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Small‑scale segment will show higher purchase intent for Deere than for the competitor, with durability and performance cited as primary reasons.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Affluent segment will show higher purchase intent for Deere than for the competitor, with status and modern lifestyle cited as primary reasons.

X1.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent for Deere in the small‑scale segment is at least 5 points higher than for the competitor, proceed to develop a small‑scale consumer proposition. If the average purchase intent for Deere in the affluent segment is at least 5 points higher than for the competitor, proceed to develop an affluent‑focused consumer proposition. If neither segment’s intent is at least 5 points higher, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.

arguments.name: Segmented Purchase Intent Test
arguments.method: Online survey with randomized exposure to a Deere lawn tractor description and a competitor lawn tractor description. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three segments: small-scale landscaping/hobby farming (n=200), affluent homeowners (n=200), and general consumers (n=200). Each segment sees its assigned description and a brief description of the competitor model. The survey measures purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and stated reason for choosing the product.
arguments.sample: 800 respondents (400 per segment) recruited from a panel representing the target demographics (small‑scale users, affluent homeowners, and general consumers).
arguments.measure: Purchase intent score for Deere versus competitor in each segment.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Small‑scale segment will show higher purchase intent for Deere than for the competitor, with durability and performance cited as primary reasons.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Affluent segment will show higher purchase intent for Deere than for the competitor, with status and modern lifestyle cited as primary reasons.

arguments.decision_rule: If the average purchase intent for Deere in the small‑scale segment is at least 5 points higher than for the competitor, proceed to develop a small‑scale consumer proposition. If the average purchase intent for Deere in the affluent segment is at least 5 points higher than for the competitor, proceed to develop an affluent‑focused consumer proposition. If neither segment’s intent is at least 5 points higher, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.
